title: Cookie Policy | Lunidex
main:
Cookie and Local Storage Policy

Last updated and effective: September 9, 2026

This page describes the cookies, local storage and measurement integrations actually used by Lunidex.

Optional measurement integrations initialize with collection disabled and capture no data before you choose. You can change or withdraw your choice at any time.

TABLE OF CONTENTS

1. Necessary and optional elements
2. Local storage
3. Optional measurement
4. Managing choices
5. Contact
1. Necessary and optional elements
Element	Purpose	Indicative lifetime
primedex-lang	Remember the selected language	1 year
primedex-consent-v2	Remember measurement choices	Until changed or deleted
primedex-product-measurement-consent	Let the server respect the PostHog choice	1 year or until withdrawn
Neon Auth cookies	Maintain the account session	According to Neon Auth configuration
Sentry error monitoring	Technical error and availability monitoring	According to Sentry retention settings
Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights and Sentry performance/replay	Audience and performance measurement after consent	After consent, according to provider settings
Neon and PostHog product measurement	TCG counters, pageviews, explicit events, errors and performance after consent	According to provider settings
2. Local storage

localStorage and sessionStorage are used for consent, session markers and technical application state. IndexedDB may contain a cache of public Pokémon and TCG responses. Local storage is not described as the durable location for your synchronized personal workspace.

3. Optional measurement

Vercel Web Analytics, Speed Insights and Sentry browser tracing or Session Replay load only if you grant the audience and performance choice. Replay masks text and inputs, blocks marked areas, and excludes network bodies and headers. The PostHog SDK is initialized opted out and sends no data before consent. Neon receives limited, aggregated TCG product measurement, and PostHog receives normalized pageviews, explicit events, limited errors and performance data if you grant the separate product measurement choice. PostHog then uses a consent-gated persistent technical identity for anonymous → account continuity; it does not receive the email or name, and it resets on logout. Replay is sampled and privacy-marked UI is blocked. Neither choice is required for public pages.

4. Managing choices

Use the Manage preferences button in the footer, or clear site data in your browser. Clearing storage may remove local preferences and close your session; synchronized data remains associated with the account according to the configured service.

5. Contact

For questions about this policy, email contact@lunidex.app.

Measurement

With your choices, Vercel Web Analytics and Speed Insights measure audience and performance. Optional Neon and PostHog product measurement sends predefined TCG events, normalized page views, and limited error/performance context. An authenticated technical account ID may continue an anonymous PostHog session; email, names and secrets are excluded. Replay is consent-gated, sampled and masked. You can withdraw at any time.

This legal document is primarily drafted in French and English. The French version prevails in case of discrepancy, subject to the mandatory provisions of your country of residence.

What is confirmed so far?

Pokémon TCG 30th Anniversary launched worldwide on September 16, 2026. Every booster includes one of 30 Pikachu cards, and the set features foil cards throughout, including Basic Energy. This page keeps the full checklist usable even when a provider record or image is temporarily unavailable.

CONFIRMED EXPANSION DETAILS

Confirmed expansion details
Worldwide release

Pokémon TCG 30th Anniversary is planned for simultaneous worldwide release on September 16, 2026.

Booster contents

Each booster is set to include five foil cards, including one of the 30 unique Pikachu illustrations, plus one foil Basic Energy card.

30 Pikachu rare cards

The confirmed Pikachu rare cards have special Pikachu numbering. Each has a unique illustration, artist, and attacks.

Two Pikachu ex reveals

Two Pikachu ex special illustration rares have been revealed and use the expansion's day and night visual theme.

Foil cards and a new rarity

The official overview describes foil cards throughout the expansion, including Basic Energy, and names Futuristic Rare as a new rarity for the set.

Classic Collection

Classic cards return for the celebration. Pokémon says those reprints are not Standard legal, while formats that allow the original editions can still use them.

THE 30 PIKACHU CARDS

The 30 Pikachu cards

The 30 confirmed Pikachu rare cards use special Pikachu numbering from 01 to 30, corresponding to set numbers 023–052. Each card has its own illustration and illustrator. The same collection records power this tracker and the general checklist below.

Mark the cards you own. The tracker writes to the same language-specific TCG collection used by the rest of Lunidex, so progress is available from your collection workspace after sign-in.

USAGE GUIDE

How to Organize a Pokémon Card Collection

Start with a physical arrangement you can maintain, then mirror it in a list with one record per card version. This guide works for a small binder or a larger set-by-set collection.

PUBLISHED SEP 28, 2026 · CHECKED AGAINST LUNIDEX SOURCE AND PUBLIC ROUTES ON SEP 28, 2026.

Lunidex editorial

Short answer

To organize Pokémon cards, choose a sorting rule you can keep using—usually by set, then collector number. Protect the cards, record each version’s language and finish, count duplicates separately, and update a missing-card list after every change. A spreadsheet, paper checklist, or collection tool can hold that list; choose based on the fields and access you need.

What this guide covers

This is a collection workflow, not a card-identification or grading service. Set codes and collector numbers make records easier to reconcile with catalogs; language, finish, condition, and quantity describe the copy you actually own.

How to use these features
01

Choose a goal: one set, one Pokémon, a language, or your whole collection. Pick a location and sorting rule before moving cards.

02

Protect cards in sleeves and store them in binders or boxes. Group by set, then by collector number; keep promos or cards outside the numbered sequence in a separate section.

03

Create one list entry for each set and card number. Add the card name, language, finish, quantity, and a note for condition or storage location if those details matter to you.

04

Mark missing cards and duplicates separately. After opening packs or trading, update the same list and review it before buying more cards.

Example record

For a fictional entry, write: SET · 025 · Pikachu · English · reverse holo · quantity 2 · binder B, page 4. If you also own a Japanese normal card with the same name and number, give it a separate entry. The set code and number identify the printing; language, finish, and quantity describe your copies.

Collection organization checklist
• Decide the scope and choose one sorting rule before rearranging cards.
• Use sleeves, then group physical cards by set and collector number.
• Record set code, card number, card name, language, and finish separately.
• Count duplicates as quantities; do not let a different language or finish share the same record.
• Keep missing cards in a separate list so a want list does not look owned.
• Update the list after packs, trades, or sales, and keep a backup.
Boundaries and practical limits

A checklist records what you entered; it does not verify card authenticity, physical condition, or current market price. Card variants and numbering can differ by printing, so compare the exact card rather than relying on the name alone.
